# wechart tasks

Inputs: [`docs/spec.md`](./spec.md) (180 acceptance criteria, F1–F21), [`docs/research/`](./research/), [`docs/design/direction.md`](./design/direction.md).

185 tasks. Every AC is covered by at least one task, and every task cites at least one AC; the coverage table at the end lists all 180. Tasks are ordered by dependency first, then by user value. `[P]` means the task depends on no unfinished task at the point it appears, so it can run in parallel with its neighbours.

**Format.** Each task line follows the shape CLAUDE.md defines, with `Files`, `Failing test` and `Depends on` sub-bullets. `[P]` marks a task whose dependencies are already met where it appears.

**Order.** Task numbers group the work by feature; the real order is the `Depends on` graph, which is acyclic. Thirteen tasks depend on a higher-numbered task (for example T023 on T071, T088 on T113) — always take the next unchecked task whose dependencies are met, never the next number.

**Working rules.** One task, one observable behaviour, one commit, message `T00N: <title> (AC-…)`. Write the failing test first, confirm it fails for the right reason, then the code. Tick an AC in `docs/spec.md` only when a passing test demonstrates it.

**`--passWithNoTests` is temporary.** The scaffold gives each package a `test` script before it has tests, so the flag keeps `pnpm test` green. It also turns a mistyped include glob into a silent pass, so drop it from a package's `test` script in the same commit as that package's first test. Scaffold tasks cite the ACs they first make testable.

**Package layout** (created by T001):

| Package                | Contents                                                                                   |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `packages/core`        | chart spec, marking model, filter model, canonical Cube query builder — no DOM, no React   |
| `packages/api`         | Fastify service: Cube proxy, metadata persistence, jobs, connection tests                  |
| `packages/web`         | Vite + React app: shell, Explore, chart editor, dashboards, model editor, admin workspaces |
| `packages/charts`      | ECharts renderer for the chart spec, plus the marking/hit-test layer                       |
| `packages/ui`          | in-house primitives and design tokens                                                      |
| `packages/recommender` | legality rules and weighted scoring                                                        |
| `e2e`                  | Playwright acceptance tests                                                                |

## F2. wechart service: Cube access, metadata and persistence

- [x] T010 (AC-009) Serve metadata from the new model within 60 seconds of a `schemaVersion` change
  - Files: `packages/api/src/cube/meta-cache.ts`, `packages/api/src/cube/meta-cache.test.ts`, `packages/api/src/server.ts`
  - Failing test: `meta-cache.test.ts`: with a fake clock, a changed `schemaVersion` causes the next metadata request after at most 60 s to return the new model's members, with no process restart (AC-009).
  - Depends on: T004
  - Done 2026-09-19. AC-009 ticked. Research correction: `schemaVersion` is a Cube **config hook** (`fn(ctx) => string`, called per request, recompiling when the string changes — `research/cube/configuration-deployment.md` §3), not something Cube pushes to clients. So the 60-second bound is wechart's own: a cached entry older than that is refetched before being served.
  - Caching is what makes the bound necessary. Without it metadata is never stale, but a ten-tile dashboard becomes ten `/v1/meta` requests against a queue whose default concurrency is 2. Concurrent callers share one in-flight fetch for the same reason.
  - `invalidate()` skips the bound for wechart's own publishes (T142/T143): waiting out 60 seconds is the wrong answer to "did my change take effect?". Failures are never cached.
- [x] T011 (AC-010) Hold the request open while Cube replies "Continue wait"
  - Files: `packages/web/src/query/{loadTile,useTileData}.ts`, `packages/web/src/query/{loadTile,useTileData}.test.ts|tsx`
  - Failing test: `loadTile.test.ts`: two "Continue wait" responses followed by a result leave the tile in its loading state throughout and then render the result, with no error state (AC-010).
  - Depends on: T004
  - Done 2026-09-19. AC-010 ticked. Cube answers a still-running query with HTTP **200** and a body of `{"error":"Continue wait"}` — an error-shaped body that is not an error. Trusting the status code renders an empty tile; trusting the word "error" shows a red tile for a query that is merely slow. Both are the failure this criterion names, so the sentinel is matched explicitly and a test asserts the tile never passes through an error state on the way.
  - The request id is minted once and carried across the whole poll, so Cube sees one query rather than a series — and so T012 has something to name when it cancels.
  - The poll is bounded (`maxPolls`), because a tile that hangs forever is its own failure. Retries are off in the hook: a Cube error is something the tile shows (AC-012), and backoff would hide it and spend AC-175's budget.
- [x] T012 (AC-011) Cancel a superseded query against Cube before rendering the newer result
  - Files: `packages/web/src/query/loadTile.ts`, `packages/web/src/query/cancel.test.ts`, `packages/api/src/cube/client.ts`, `packages/api/src/server.ts`, `packages/api/src/server.test.ts`
  - Failing test: `cancel.test.ts`: changing a tile's filters aborts the in-flight fetch and issues `DELETE /v1/running-query/{requestId}` for it, and the older result never replaces the newer one (AC-011).
  - Depends on: T011
  - Done 2026-09-19. AC-011 ticked. **Dropping the response is not cancelling** — the criterion says "against Cube". An abandoned query keeps running and holds one of the queue's two default slots until its orphan timeout, so a user dragging a filter slider can starve their own dashboard. The abort listener fires `DELETE /api/running-query/{id}`, which the service forwards to Cube.
  - A test asserts the cancellation names the id the load actually used: one naming a fresh id stops nothing, and would pass a weaker assertion.
  - The route always answers 204, including when Cube says the query is unknown. The tile that issued it is already gone and a failed cancellation is not something anyone can act on; the warning goes to the log.
- [x] T013 (AC-012) Show a tile error state carrying Cube's message and the query JSON
  - Files: `packages/web/src/tiles/TileError.tsx`, `packages/web/src/tiles/TileError.test.tsx`
  - Failing test: `TileError.test.tsx`: a Cube error renders the message and a control that reveals the exact query JSON sent, instead of an empty chart (AC-012).
  - Depends on: T011
  - Done 2026-09-19. AC-012 ticked. Cube's message is shown **verbatim** rather than translated into something friendlier: "Can't find join path between Orders and Suppliers" tells an author what to change, where "Something went wrong" tells them to file a ticket. A test asserts the original message survives.
  - The query JSON is one control away — the other half of diagnosing a failure, but noise while the message is enough. The state pairs an icon with a label, never colour alone.
- [x] T014 (AC-013) Mark a tile accelerated with a data age, or live
  - Files: `packages/web/src/tiles/AccelerationBadge.tsx`, `packages/web/src/tiles/AccelerationBadge.test.tsx`

  - Depends on: T011

Both directions are asserted, because both mislead: labelling everything "live" hides that a number is an hour old, and labelling everything "accelerated" claims a freshness guarantee that is not there (requirements §4 — volumes vary widely, so the UI has to say which queries are accelerated).

    - Web:
      - `query/answerMeta.ts` (`answerMetaOf`) and its test. What Cube says of an answer besides its rows is `lastRefreshTime` and `usedPreAggregations`. It is carried as one `answered` record wherever the answer goes, replacing T154's `asOf`: the page's load, a refresh, a filtered answer, and a save with drafts.

    - The Cube stack:
      - `docker-compose.yml`: a `cube-refresh-worker` service with the same image and configuration as the API instance, plus `CUBEJS_REFRESH_WORKER=true`.
      - `infra/cube/cube.js`: `scheduledRefreshContexts`, covering the mounted model and each trusted store's.
      - A seed cube, `infra/cube/model/cubes/monthly_orders.yml`. It has a rollup of count and total by status and month, partitioned by year, with an index on status. It is a cube of its own with no joins, so nothing else the sample model answers changes. It gives F16 a rollup to list, rebuild and index.
    - **Why the worker.** Observed locally: in production mode, a Cube API instance with no refresh worker answers HTTP 400 to any query a rollup would serve until the rollup is built ("this API instance wasn't set up to build pre-aggregations"). With the worker, the rollup was built 24–30 s after start. Recorded in `research/cube/pre-aggregations.md`, "Observed locally".

      - Written out, the two badges left a half-width tile's title one letter wide at 1280 px, and pushed "Table view" under the corner controls. They are now shown as the prototype's tile badge is (`✓ 3m` in `prototype/dashboard.js`): "⚡ 16m" and "as of 11:01:13 PM". The whole sentences are the badges' text for a screen reader, and their tooltips; the tooltip also names the rollup. `e2e/acceleration.spec.ts` now checks the title keeps at least 96 px and "Table view" ends before ↻.
      - A test that a filtered tile's badge comes from its filtered answer (above).
      - Stale notes corrected (T137's note about the seed model, and the badge's comment on an absent `usedPreAggregations`).
      - Left as found: the relative age is worked out when the tile draws, so "16m" doesn't count up on an open dashboard. The absolute time beside it stays true. The Jobs log names a rollup by its table, where the tile uses the model's name.
    - AC-013 stays ticked, now on the real surface: `e2e/acceleration.spec.ts`, against the real Cube in all three browsers. A `monthly_orders` tile reads "Accelerated · built … ago", with its icon and the rollup's model name. An `orders` tile reads "Live" and not "Accelerated". The test first waits for the worker to have built the rollup.

## F3. Explore: folders, catalog and search

- [x] T016 (AC-017) Show the folder tree and the selected folder's contents
  - Files: `packages/web/src/workspaces/explore/{FolderTree,FolderContents}.tsx`, `packages/api/src/routes/folders.ts`, `packages/web/src/workspaces/explore/FolderContents.test.tsx`
  - Failing test: `FolderContents.test.tsx`: every dashboard and library chart in the folder is listed with its type, owner and last-updated time, and no column is blank for an item that has that value (AC-017).
  - Depends on: T003, T005
  - Done 2026-09-19. **AC-017 and AC-003 both ticked.** The scroll half of AC-003, deferred from T007, is now in `e2e/explore.spec.ts` against a seeded list of 34 items; it asserts the page really scrolled before asserting the offset survives, so it cannot pass on a page that never moved.
  - **AC-003 genuinely failed the first time.** Not because the theme switch lost the scroll — nothing unmounted, the document height and row count were identical — but because the top bar scrolled away, so clicking the theme control made the browser scroll it back into view. The fix is a sticky bar, which a workbench wants regardless: the switcher, search and theme stay reachable however far a surface has scrolled.
  - Columns for the listing are **generated** from `body` in Postgres rather than written beside it, so a rename cannot leave the listing stale; a test covers exactly that.
  - Two infrastructure changes this task forced: the API now builds with Vite and runs as its own process in `playwright.config.ts` (Node's `--experimental-strip-types` does no module resolution, so it wants an explicit `.ts` on every relative import); and **the tests now use their own database**. Sharing one with development let test fixtures into the catalog the app listed, and the dev seed then saw folders nobody had created and skipped itself.

    - **One transaction, on the server.** A dashboard save that carries chart edits goes to `PUT /api/dashboards/:id` with `{ dashboard: {body, version}, charts: [{id, body, version}] }`; a save with none still uses `PUT /api/documents/dashboard/:id`, unchanged. The repository's `updateTogether` writes every document in one READ COMMITTED transaction, each checked against the version it was read at, in (kind, id) order so two saves touching the same documents take their locks in the same order; any failure rolls back all of them and rethrows the same error (`docs/research/db-access.md`, "Query-time transactions"). Proven against the real Postgres: a non-transactional version failed the rollback test, and the transactional one passes. The race test passes without the transaction too — it proves the version check, not atomicity, and is recorded as such.
    - **The dashboard-save route refuses what the client holds back**, by the same rule (`refusalOf` in the client): a library chart → 400, a chart local to another dashboard → 400, and a body that would move a chart to another dashboard → 400. Locality is judged only at the version the client read — a mismatch is a 409 at once — so a client cannot have its write judged by a locality nobody checked. A stored chart this build cannot read → 422, as the document GET answers it. **This is not every route that writes a chart:** `PUT /api/documents/:kind/:id` writes any chart, library or not — it is the library chart's own save — so "no client can spread a change by calling the API" would be false, and the first version of this record and of the route's comment said it; both corrected at review (F2). A stale version inside the transaction → 409 naming which document (`document: {kind, id}`), which `saveDashboard` turns into a `StaleSaveError` saying whether it was the dashboard or a chart; any other refusal reaches the user with the server's own reason, not "Could not save: 400". A deadlock (`40P01`) → 409, the same "changed somewhere else" as a race. **That is a default, not a decision:** `docs/research/db-access.md` lists retry-versus-conflict as open for the user, as are statement and lock timeouts (left at Postgres's defaults). The stakes are low — every `updateTogether` locks in (kind, id) order, and a single-document write holds one lock, so no two writers here can form a cycle — but the first version of this record said "decided here", which it was not mine to say (review F12).
    - **Version carried from the first read.** `loadChart` returns the version; `ChartDraft.version` keeps it through every reopening of a drafted chart, so a second edit is still checked against the version the first was read at. A draft with no version holds Save back (`whyUnsaveable`) and `chartWritesOf` throws for one, so the two guards cannot silently disagree into a blind overwrite.

Library charts wait on T134 (AC-128), client (`whyUnsaveable`) and server (400) alike; T134's entry records what it inherits. Only drafts of charts a tile still shows count, and only those are written: a tile deleted after its chart was edited no longer holds Save back, and its chart is not written for nothing on screen.
    - **The tile keeps the edit through the save.** Saving leaves edit mode at once, before the server answers, and the drafts go with the session — so the tile fell back to the chart as loaded until the charts were fetched again. The save writes the drafts into the charts' cached query first (`onMutate`), and a failed save re-fetches them. The browser test records every chart type the tile shows from Save on; without the cache write it sees `bar` twice.

  - **The tests render, they do not inspect an option.** ECharts draws headlessly through its SSR mode (`init(null, …, { ssr: true, renderer: 'svg' })`), so each test produces a real SVG and reads the marks back out of it. AC-037 fails "when a listed type cannot be produced from a valid spec", and an option object is not a chart: a test asserting `series[0].type === 'bar'` passes just as happily when the option is unrenderable.
  - Orientation is read from where the category labels land — spread along the bottom for a bar, down the side for a horizontal bar — rather than from the option, so "horizontal" means the drawn result and not the flag we set.
  - Grouped and stacked are told apart by geometry: grouped marks occupy disjoint horizontal extents on a shared baseline, stacked marks share one column with the upper mark's foot meeting the lower one's head. Mutating the layout table so `hbar` is not horizontal and `stackedBar` is not stacked fails 4 tests, so the assertions discriminate.
  - **Rejected at cold review on the mark rules, then fixed.** The first version claimed direction.md §6 was "implemented and demonstrated" and neither half held. The gap was drawn as a 1 px border on each of two touching marks, on the assumption that two 1 px borders make 2 px — but an SVG stroke straddles the boundary the two marks share, so both strokes land in the same 1 px band. Each mark carries the **full** width. And the only assertion guarding it looked for `stroke="<surface>"` in the output, which survives a border width of 0: zrender emits `stroke` whatever the width, and omits `stroke-width` entirely when it is 1 — precisely the value the bug produced.
  - Rounding was asserted as "the outline contains an arc", which is true of a pill, of a half-pixel radius, and of a bar rounded at the baseline — the rule inverted. The helper now records each corner's radius and position, and the tests assert both. A **negative** bar grows downwards, so its data-end is its bottom; the radii follow the sign of each value, which also means they are per datum and not per series. Restoring either bug fails a test.
  - "Outermost segment" is per drawn segment, not per series: `seriesOf` emits `null` gaps, so a stack whose top series is missing in one category would otherwise get a flat top there.
  - `bar` and `groupedBar` share one layout, which the review rightly asked about. It is a decision: a grouped bar *is* a bar chart with more than one series, so grouping is a property of the data. Making `bar` refuse a second series would turn "add another measure" into an error for something the user plainly meant. A test pins the two together so they cannot quietly diverge, and so the grouped block is not read as proving something about the type that it only proves about the data.
  - The test palette is deliberately **not** the default ramp. With `DEFAULT_PALETTE[0]` and `[1]` every assertion passed even if `barOption` ignored `spec.palette` — and the palette being handed in rather than looked up is the hinge AC-039 hangs on.
  - **The chart-type vocabulary moved to `@wechart/core`**, which the recommender now re-exports. It is what a saved chart is written in, and the renderer has to agree with it; two lists would drift, and a recommendation for a type the renderer never heard of fails at draw time. The 18 names are unchanged, and `ChartSpec.chartType` is now typed as `ChartType` rather than `string` — without that the stated reason was aspirational, since a saved chart was not actually written in the vocabulary.
  - The path reader throws on any command it does not handle. Skipping one silently returns a wrong bounding box, which would make every geometry assertion in this file meaningless rather than failing.
  - A gap is `null`, never `0`: zero is a measurement and a missing row is the absence of one. Cube returns measures as JSON strings, so `seriesOf` converts them — a renderer trusting the raw value would sort and scale them as text.

  - **`Encoding` becomes a channel model** — x, y, colour, size, facet, row, column — replacing `{category, series, values[]}`, which was fitted to the bar and line families and cannot express scatter (two value axes), heatmap (two categories plus colour), treemap (hierarchy plus size), pivot (rows × columns × measures) or trellis (a facet). The value axis genuinely takes several — a grouped bar of two measures — and Metabase's `graph.dimensions`/`graph.metrics` are both arrays for the same reason. One shape beats a union of singular and plural channels that every caller would have to know about.

## F11. Details tiles and marked-rows actions

- [x] T113 (AC-107) Limit a tile by markings, combined as AND or OR, skipping empty markings
  - Files: `packages/core/src/markings/limit-by.ts`, `packages/core/src/markings/limit-by.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/index.ts`
  - Failing test: `limit-by.test.ts`: two limiting markings with one empty return the rows of the non-empty one, and OR returns the union where AND returns the intersection (AC-107).
  - Depends on: T092
  - Done 2026-09-20. AC-107 ticked.
  - **The skip-empty rule is ours, and direction.md flags it as such**: "Proposed rule, not from Spotfire's docs." It matters because the naive reading is catastrophic under AND — a details tile limited by two markings, where the user has marked in only one, would intersect against an empty set and show nothing. The tile goes blank exactly when someone starts working, and the remedy ("also mark something in the other master tile") is not a thing anyone would guess. Mutation-verified.
  - **Nothing marked anywhere returns every row, not none.** What the tile then *shows* is a per-tile setting — All data, an empty visualisation, or a message, with the message the default — so the decision belongs to whoever renders it. Returning nothing here would make "All data" impossible to implement.
  - Rows come back by identity and in their original order: the tile's own sort is the tile's business, and identity is what lets a renderer tell whether a row actually changed rather than repainting everything on each marking change.
  - **Connected 2026-09-23 — and the limit went into the query, not into the rows.** `limitRowsBy` filters rows that Cube has already aggregated, so a limited tile using it would draw the marked rows with every total computed over *everything*: a "total" that is not the total of what is shown. `packages/core/src/markings/query.ts` converts the predicate to a Cube filter instead (single-member items collapse to one `equals`, multi-member tuples become an OR of ANDs, ranges become `gte`/`lte`), which `FilteredCharts` appends to `query.filters` — where Cube ANDs the entries, which is AC-082 with no second mechanism. Nested `{or}`/`{and}` are supported per `docs/research/cube/data-apis.md`; that research also warns that dimension and measure filters may not share a logical operator, so a range over a measure is left for the caller to place. Evidence: `e2e/markings.spec.ts` "a limited tile shows only what is marked" and "an empty marking limiting a tile is skipped, not intersected". AC-107 re-ticked.
  - **A limited tile is asked even when no filter reaches it**, and its limit is never dropped to rescue a refused query — a dashboard filter that cannot be joined is one the user did not aim at this tile, but a limit they did, and a tile that quietly dropped it would show unmarked rows in a tile whose whole purpose is to show marked ones.
  - **Three encoding rules the cold review caught, each a silent wrong answer.** A marked *time bucket* was emitted as `equals` on the raw member with the bucket's start instant — so marking a month bar asked for rows at exactly midnight on the 1st, and the details tile went quietly empty; `markings-query-support.md` §1.2 says a bucket is `inDateRange` over `["…T00:00:00.000","…T23:59:59.999"]`, which is what it now sends. A marked *NULL* became `equals ['']`, which is `col = ''` — matching empty strings and never NULLs (§1.5 says `notSet`, and §1.6 puts it in an `or` beside the other values of that member, which blocks the single-`equals` collapse). And `predicate.ts` had already written the instruction — "The task that translates a predicate into a Cube filter needs that answer and should research it" — which the first version did not follow. All four cases are now tested.
  - **One rule recorded rather than fixed:** a `BoundedRange` over a *measure* cannot share a logical operator with a dimension filter (`data-apis.md`:226), and `rangeFilter` cannot tell a measure from a dimension — only the model can. Nothing produces such a range yet, because range mode is AC-093 and unbuilt; the constraint is written at the function and in the research doc's open questions, for AC-093 to supply the member kinds.
  - **The filter is canonical, which is what earns AC-105.** Values within an `equals`, members within an item and branches within a marking are sorted by their own JSON, so the same *set* of marks is the same query however it was clicked. Unsorted, clicking A then B and B then A were two cache entries for one question, and the second went to the database for an answer already in memory. Evidence: `e2e/markings.spec.ts` "the same set of marks asks Cube the same question, whatever order it was marked in", which compares the bodies the page actually sent.
  - **The `/jobs` contrast flake, sixth sighting, with two hypotheses eliminated.** Stressing `a11y-tokens.spec.ts` alone — 216 runs at 6 workers — passes every time, so it is contention with the *rest* of the suite rather than a timing problem inside that spec. And the query log's error text, the obvious content that only appears once other specs have run, carries no colour rule at all (`.query-log__error` and `[data-icon]` are unstyled), so it is not that either. Still uncaptured; next attempt should snapshot axe's violation from a full-suite run rather than re-testing the spec in isolation.

  - **Why the rule exists, recorded because the control looks arbitrary without it.** A tile limited by its own marking feeds back on itself: marking two bars restricts the tile to those two bars, the others vanish, and with them any way to change the marking. The tile locks itself, and the only escape is a settings page the user has no reason to connect to what just happened.
  - **"Prevent" is stronger than "do not offer", so it is enforced twice** — the control disables the option, and `allowedLimits` drops it from any stored list. A document can arrive hand-edited or from a build predating the rule, and a UI that merely hid the option would apply it anyway, locking the tile with no control on screen to unlock it. Both guards are independently mutation-verified.
  - **The reason sits beside the option**, as the criterion requires ("where that option is offered"). A disabled control with no explanation is the most frustrating kind: the user cannot tell whether it is broken, forbidden, or waiting on something they have not done. Options that are *not* disabled carry no explanation, or people learn to skip the one that matters.
  - `allowedLimits` returns its input by identity when nothing had to be removed, so a document that was already valid is not rewritten — which would make the edit session think it had changed.

So on a real dashboard nothing was barred: the e2e found the own-marking checkbox enabled on the master tile. `TileLimits` now resolves the default the way `TileMarking` does, and `DashboardView` resolves it before calling `allowedLimits`. AC-108 re-ticked on `e2e/markings.spec.ts` "a tile cannot be limited by the marking it marks with, and is told why".
  - **The limit checkboxes are named "Limit by &lt;marking&gt;".** Beside the tile's "Marking" picker, a checkbox whose whole accessible name is the marking's name is a second control carrying the first one's name — neither a screen reader nor a test can tell them apart. The visible text is still the marking's name, so the accessible name contains it (WCAG 2.5.3).
  - **Labels are tied by `id`, not by wrapping.** A `<label>` around a `<select>` takes its options into the accessible name, so "When nothing is marked" was really "When nothing is markedAll dataEmpty visualization…" — which no exact query can reach, and which a screen reader reads out in full.

- [x] T123 (AC-117) Apply the configured action for each source and target pair
  - Files: `packages/web/src/dashboard/crossfilter/apply.ts`, `packages/web/src/dashboard/crossfilter/apply.test.ts`

  - **Built 2026-09-23.**
    - **What Highlight draws — the user's decision, 2026-09-22.** Asked how a highlighted target should look, the user chose Power BI's: the tile keeps its own values, faded, and the selection's own values are drawn over them from the baseline, from a second query. Not a share of the tile's total: a measure over a subset is not a fraction of the measure over everything, which is why it is Cube's answer rather than arithmetic here. The research is `docs/research/cross-highlight.md` (written for this task; it also corrects `references.md`, which said every target offers Filter / Highlight / None — Power BI offers Highlight only where the target can show one).
    - **Where each drawing applies.** `share` on a plain bar or horizontal bar, where the selection has a slot of its own: `barGap: '-100%'` is a property of the whole grid, so on a grouped or stacked chart the overlay would land on every series at once (that research, gotcha 4). `fade` — the matching items keep their strength, the rest go back — on grouped, stacked and combo bars, pie, donut, treemap and heatmap, and only where the tile groups by the clicked member, since otherwise no item on it is the selection. Everything else (lines, area, scatter, KPI, table, pivot, trellis) is **filtered** instead, as Power BI filters lines, scatter and maps. A pair asking for a highlight a tile cannot draw filters it rather than leaving it alone: the pair asked for the selection to reach it.
    - **A cross-filter is written as a filter** (`DashboardView` `crossFilters`), scoped to the tiles the matrix says it filters, so it takes the path every dashboard filter takes: one query per tile, its reach checked against the model, and a tile whose cube cannot join to the field left unfiltered and told so — the user's second decision, and the same note AC-079 already shows.
    - **Clicking.** `mousedown` and `mouseup` paired with the existing 5 px slop (`itemClicks`), never ECharts' `click`, which `docs/research/echarts.md` finds is dropped after 4 px of movement with nothing dispatched at all. What the click stands for follows the prototype: the category on a bar or pie, the series on a grouped, stacked or multi-line chart, the panel in a trellis. One selection per tile, and the same value again takes it back, as Power BI and Superset both do.
    - **Off where it should be:** in Markings mode, while editing (a click selects the tile there), and in a previewed security context. Selections are held in the view, not in the document: clicking a mark is reading the dashboard, not changing it.
    - **Tests:**

Such a click now selects nothing.
      - **The share overlay mis-drew any bar tile with more than one series.** The gate was the chart type, but a bar chart draws one series per measure; `barGap: '-100%'` belongs to the whole grid, so the overlay would have landed on every series. It now gates on the series count, and such a tile fades or is filtered instead.
      - **A heatmap lost its cells under a fade.** Its data items are `[column, row, value]` triples, and spreading an array into an object dropped the value ECharts reads. Arrays are carried as the item's `value`, and a cell's column is matched by index.

    - **The check runs on each edit, not on the file.** Here the form and the YAML are both on screen, and a form edit is written into the file in place (T139), which keeps every comment and anchor it doesn't touch.
      - So there is no "switch" to warn about, and most edits lose nothing.
      - Each form edit is checked before it's applied. `lossOf` compares the file before and after it, collecting each node's `commentBefore` and `comment`, its `anchor`, and each alias's `source` (research/yaml.md, "Comments and anchors").
      - What `after` no longer has is named. Comments are counted line by line, so a block `yaml` writes back split or merged isn't a false loss. A comment is named by its first line.
    - **This departs from the prototype and direction.md §7b.** The prototype makes the whole form read-only for a file with comments, until "Edit in form anyway", because its form rewrote the file. Here nothing is held for an edit that loses nothing.
    - **When an edit would lose something**, it is held. The form is read-only meanwhile, and the prototype's warnbar names what would go:
      - It reads, for example: "This edit would drop the comment “Cube hides primary keys … This one …”. The YAML keeps them while you edit there."
      - "Apply anyway" writes the edit.
      - "Keep the file" leaves the file as it was.
      - Typing in the YAML drops the held edit, since it was made against the text before.
      - The bar scrolls into view and puts the focus on "Keep the file", because locking the form drops the focus from the field that was being edited.
      - **AC-134 wins over AC-133 here:** such an edit reaches the YAML when it's applied, not in the same render.
    - **An edit that can't be written at all** is refused with `yaml`'s reason. An example is removing an anchor that an alias still uses, where writing the file throws. It isn't applied, and the refusal clears on the next edit or on typing in the YAML.

      - `packages/api/src/model/{publish,validate}.ts`, with their tests and `cube-config.test.ts`;
      - `config.ts`, `cube/client.ts`, `server.ts`, `repos/model-files.ts`, `seed.ts`;

      - `docker-compose.yml` and `playwright.config.ts`.
      - There is no `routes/model.ts`: the routes are registered from `model/publish.ts`.
    - **`cube.js`: where Cube reads the model.**
      - It reads from the store named in the request's signed security context (`wechartStore`), and only if that store is on `WECHART_MODEL_STORES`. Otherwise it reads the mounted directory, as Cube did before.
      - A `wechartDraft` compiles a draft under its own app id.
      - The store is asked for its version on every request. A version kept even for a second hid a publish (T143).
      - Idle compiled models expire after ten minutes (`maxCompilerCacheKeepAlive`, reset on use), so drafts don't pile up in Cube's memory.
      - Observed through a throwaway Cube (research spike §1a).
    - **One Cube, several wechart instances.** The compose Cube trusts the dev and browser-test API (:4100) and the demo (:4200). Each instance's tokens name its own store, so each reads its own model.
    - **API routes for Cube** (`/api/cube-model/{files,version,drafts/:id}`), behind a shared key (`WECHART_MODEL_KEY`, compared timing-safely):
      - With no key, no one is served.
      - A store address without a key fails the start.
      - The version is worked out from the store on each ask, since another instance may have published.
    - **Publish (`POST /api/model/publish`):**
      - Only YAML files, by plain paths. Nothing with Jinja markers, and no stored template written over.
      - The whole model with the changes goes to Cube as a draft, through `/v1/meta` with the draft named.
      - It is published only if Cube read the draft and compiled it.
      - Cube's refusal (a 500, draft read) comes back as 422 with its errors attributed per file.
      - Cube failing without reading the draft, or answering from another model, is a 502, not a refusal of the file.
      - On success the files are written and the metadata cache let go of.
    - **Attribution (`validate.ts`):**
      - A compile-errors group names its file.
      - An undefined name goes on the changed file that holds it.
      - A YAML error goes on the changed file whose line its snippet shows.
      - Otherwise, each changed file: the live model compiled, so the error is in the change.
    - **The page:** "Save & reload Cube", the prototype's label, in the editor head.
      - It is enabled when the text has changed, parses, and has been read by the form, with nothing held.
      - On success: "Published. Cube is reading the new model.", and the listing and every field list are refetched.
      - On refusal: "Cube refused the model, so nothing was published.", with Cube's reasons in the Problems panel as "Cube: …" on their files.
    - **Browser-test isolation.** The browsers run at once and each publish writes a whole file, so a test that publishes successfully does so on a cube file of its own, created through the API (`e2e/model-files.ts`).
      - `WECHART_RESET_DATA` also clears the model, which is seeded again from the directory.

    - **Why the model files, not `/v1/meta`.** Cube's `/v1/meta` leaves hidden members out, even with `?extended=true`, and a rollup may name them: a `public: false` dimension and the primary key both matched. Names are resolved as Cube resolved them in the probes: bare, `CUBE.`, `TABLE.` and the cube's own name are its own cube's; `other.member` is another cube's; a join path (`CUBE.customers.country`) is the member of the cube it ends at; and a cube has what it `extends`. Only an index column may carry a granularity. That rollup's row reads "⚠ Not in the model, so not published: `CUBE.no_such_member` (dimensions)", and a name drops off as soon as the rollup stops writing it. The refusal is kept in session storage for the tab, because each model file opens as a page of its own, so a rollup in another file shows it when that file is opened. It is cleared by the next successful publish.

  - Files: `packages/web/src/editor/AccelerationPanel.tsx`, `packages/api/src/cube/preaggMatch.ts`, `packages/api/src/cube/preaggMatch.test.ts`
  - Failing test: `preaggMatch.test.ts`: a matching query reports the rollup Cube actually uses, and a non-matching one names the member that blocks the match (AC-144).

  - **Done 2026-09-21.** Files as built:
    - API: `cube/preaggMatch.ts` (`rollupsFrom`, `missOf`) and its test; `cube/client.ts` (`sql`, `dryRun`, `metaExtended`); `server.ts` (`POST /api/acceleration`), tested in `server.test.ts`.

  - **Whether it matches is Cube's word.** `/v1/sql` plans the query without running it and names the pre-aggregations it would use, by `preAggregationId`. The panel reports that and nothing else. So it can't report a match Cube doesn't use, which is the first half of the Fails-when.
  - **Why it misses** is worked out from what Cube matches on: the dry run's transformed query, against the rollups Cube compiled (`/v1/meta?extended=true`). It follows the matcher's additive rules (`research/cube/pre-aggregations.md` §2):
    - every leaf measure, dimension and filtered member must be in the rollup;
    - each time dimension must be the rollup's, at a granularity Cube's own `granularityHierarchies` says the rollup's can make;
    - a measure that doesn't add up needs a rollup grouped exactly as the query.

    The rollup reported is the one with the fewest members missing, and the member named is the first that stops it. A cube with no rollups says so, naming the chart's first measure. If every member is in the nearest rollup and Cube still didn't use it, the panel says so, naming the time dimension. That points at the date range or the time zone, which the rules above don't cover. So a miss always names a member. The shapes of all three answers were observed on the local Cube, and are recorded under "Observed locally".
  - AC-144 ticked, on the real Cube in all three browsers (`e2e/preaggregations.spec.ts`):
    - The seed cube's count by status reads "Served from the pre-aggregation monthly_orders.by_status_month.", and `/api/load` confirms Cube serves that chart from that rollup.
    - Adding `ordered_at`, which every chart asks by day, reads a miss: the nearest rollup, and `monthly_orders.ordered_at` "is grouped by day, and the rollup keeps it by month". `/api/load` confirms Cube answers it from the database.
    - A chart on `orders` reads "orders has no pre-aggregations".
  - **Cold review (one round, 2026-09-21), verdict FAIL.** A chart touching a joined cube had its reason blamed on a member the rollup holds. Fixed, with each of Cube's shapes checked on the local Cube first (`research/cube/pre-aggregations.md`, "How the dry run spells what it owns"):
    - **Joined members.** The dry run spells a joined cube's member by its join path (`orders.customers.country`), and the model spells it `customers.country`. Members are now compared by their own cube and name (the last two segments), and hierarchies are looked up the same way. Rollups are looked for on every cube the query involves, the joined ones included, as Cube searches them.
    - **Filters.** The extra pass over the query's raw filters is gone. A filtered dimension is already among the dry run's owned dimensions, by its cube name. A filtered measure is not, so it is no longer blamed. A blocking dimension that is filtered on still says so.
    - **Segments.** A rollup's `segmentReferences` count among what it can serve, since a query's segments are among its owned dimensions.
    - **Date ranges.** A rollup that allows non-strict date ranges (Cube's default) is matched on the time dimensions as asked (`ownedTimeDimensionsAsIs`), and a strict one on the granularity a range needs. A date range with no grouping is no longer read as "grouped by day". A range that isn't whole periods, for a strict rollup, now says so.

It adds "while the worker keeps up — longer while it is busy". That was measured: under the e2e suite's load the rebuild came 2–3 minutes after the turn-over, as the research's bound (plus the time a run takes to reach the partition) allows. The e2e holds the rebuild to follow the turn-over and come within the 5½-minute bound. It times the rebuild after the new key's first build: the default key's build can land minutes before the publish while the form is used, and the new key's first build comes when the worker next reads it, not at a minute's turn. Timed from the default build, a full run failed once in Firefox by 40 s.

    - e2e: `e2e/jobs.spec.ts`.
    - **From Cube's own probes.** `/readyz` and `/livez` need no auth, sit outside the API's base path, and answer `HEALTH` or `DOWN` (`research/cube/refresh-jobs-caching.md` §F).
      - The API instance is probed at its origin. The refresh worker, observed to answer its own probes, is probed at `CUBE_WORKER_URL`.
      - Each reads healthy only if both its probes say `HEALTH`. A `DOWN`, a non-200, an error, or no answer within 3 s reads down.
      - Without `CUBE_WORKER_URL` the worker reads "not watched", never "running".
    - **In the Jobs header**, as the prototype's "Refresh worker running" badge: "Cube healthy" or "Cube down", and "Refresh worker running", "down" or "not watched". Each is an icon and words, asked again every 10 s while the page is open.
      - A health that can't be read reads "unknown", not the last answer. The query kept that answer after a later ask failed, and it would have gone on saying healthy.
    - AC-156 ticked:
      - `e2e/jobs.spec.ts`, in all three browsers: on the real stack the header reads "Cube healthy" (ok icon) and "Refresh worker running", and the API's own answer agrees. With the API answering down, the header reads "Cube down" (failed icon) and "Refresh worker down".
      - `cube/health.test.ts`: Cube not ready, not live, unreachable, or 200 without `HEALTH` all read down.
      - `Health.test.tsx`: the header moves from healthy to down while open.
    - **Cold review (one round, 2026-09-22), verdict PASS. Fixed:**
      - **The probe's time limit is tested**, against a real server that takes the request and never answers: down, within the limit. Also against real servers answering `DOWN`, a 503 that still says `HEALTH` (down), and `HEALTH` (healthy). The limit can be set in a test.
      - **The e2e leaves the page open** and waits for the header's own poll to read down, rather than reloading.
      - **An answer the page doesn't know** (a new state, or none) reads "unknown", rather than breaking the page.
      - **`CUBE_WORKER_URL` must be an http(s) URL**, or the API refuses to start. Otherwise every probe fails, and the worker reads down forever.
      - **The worker's port is published on 127.0.0.1 only**, since it serves Cube's whole REST API, not just its probes.
      - The research's UNVERIFIED note on the worker's probes now points to the observation.
      - Left as found: behind a proxy that adds a path prefix, the probes at Cube's origin would 404 and read down (safe, never a false healthy). "Refresh worker running" means its process and connections are up, not that its builds succeed.

    - **Research, observed first:** each predefined granularity was asked of the running Cube, and what comes back was recorded in `research/cube/data-apis.md` ("The values that come back"). The bucket's start arrives as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSS` with no offset, in the query's time zone. It arrives twice, under `member` and under `member.<granularity>`. Weeks start on Monday. From the installed ECharts source, `research/echarts.md` now records that a category axis's and a legend's formatter are called with the raw name.
    - **Core:**
      - `TimeGranularity` and `MemberGranularities` are new types.
      - `formatterFor` and `formatValue` take the granularities and write a time member by its granularity: "2026", "Q1 2026", "Jan 2026", "Week of Jan 5, 2026", "Jan 2, 2026", and "Jan 2, 2026, 3:04 PM" for an hour or a minute (with seconds for a second).
      - The value is read as written and formatted in UTC, so a reader in another zone sees the bucket Cube named. The time of day is written out by hand, because Intl's en-US time puts a narrow no-break space before "PM" in newer ICU and a plain space in older.
      - `granularityOf` also recognises the `member.<granularity>` column.
      - `RenderSpec.granularities` is filled by `compile` from the chart's time dimensions through `granularitiesOf`. It shares `QUERY_GRANULARITY` (day) with `toCubeQuery`, so the rows' bucket and their labels cannot disagree.
      - The model's own strftime format for a time member is T201's to honour. Until then the granularity's form stands in, never the raw timestamp.

A release that no item took is a click on empty plot area, which unmarks that tile's marking — observed on the wrapper's `mouseup`, because `pointerup` fires *before* ECharts dispatches and every click on a mark would otherwise look like a click on nothing.
    - The badge on the tile and the chip on the bar name the marking and its count in words (AC-098); the change is announced politely with its count and the tile it came from (AC-101).
    - `useThemeName` was added beside `useTheme`: a marking's colour is a value ECharts paints with, and a surface rendered without a provider should still draw rather than fail over a colour it could default.
    - **Tests:** `charts/src/marking/option.test.ts` (own colour kept, marking-coloured outline, unmarked faded, by series where a dimension splits them, nothing when the marking is empty) and `e2e/markings.spec.ts` on a real two-tile dashboard: a click marks and fades the rest, the outline appears, the badge and chip say so, the announcement carries the count, a plain click replaces while Ctrl-click adds and removes, and a click on empty plot area unmarks.
    - **Ticked here: AC-087, AC-096, AC-098, AC-101.** AC-094 waits for Escape on a focused tile (its other half, with the keyboard work); AC-095 for a second tile using the same marking across page tabs.
  - **Stage 2, 2026-09-23: the tile's Marking setting (T091), and across page tabs.**
    - The marking is read at render from one place, so a tile on a page tab that was never open while the marking changed draws it the moment that tab is opened — which is AC-095's failing state, and the reason the state is held for the dashboard rather than pushed to tiles.
    - **Ticked here: AC-085, AC-095**, both on `e2e/markings.spec.ts`: a marking made on one page showing on a tile of a page opened afterwards, and the Marking setting on a real tile including "(None)", which then marks nothing.
  - **Stage 3, 2026-09-23: the legend, and a table's rows.**
    - **A legend entry marks its whole category** rather than hiding the series (AC-090), and Ctrl there *adds* a category where Ctrl on an item toggles one — the criteria differ, and Spotfire behaves the same way round.
    - **Read from the DOM, not from ECharts' legend events.** `selectedMode: false` is what stops a legend click hiding a series, and with it no legend mouse event arrived; a marking gesture that sometimes does nothing is worse than none. A release no mark took is matched against what the legend lists — the spec's own series names — and is otherwise a click on empty plot area.
    - **A table's rows mark, and Shift extends from the anchor** (AC-092). `DataTable` has had the behaviour since T098 and no caller ever passed it a marking; it does now. Rows are markable only where the cube declares a primary key, which `primaryKeyOf` reads from `/v1/meta` — a column that happens to be unique in one answer is not an identity. The lookup is done where the rest of the model is read, in `DashboardPage`, rather than querying again inside the dashboard.
    - **Tests:** `markings/primaryKey.test.ts` (the key, a cube without one, a hidden key, and no model yet) and `e2e/markings.spec.ts` — a legend click marking a category without changing how many marks are drawn, Ctrl adding a second, a row click marking one row and Shift-click marking the range.
    - **Ticked here: AC-090, AC-092.**
  - **Stage 4, 2026-09-23: trellis panel headers (AC-091).**
    - A panel's header marks every item in that panel: the facet value alone, which is what makes "every item" true whatever else varies inside it. The titles already carried `triggerEvent` for this, from T195.
    - **The panel is taken by its index, not by the words shown.** A panel of time is titled by its granularity ("Jan 2026"), so the title is not the value; the index is matched against the facet's own values in the order the panels were drawn.
    - **Tests:** `e2e/markings.spec.ts` — a header click marking the panel's category and fading the other panel's bars. The fixture names the facet in the chart's `encoding`, because two dimensions alone compile to an axis and a colour split, never to panels.
    - **Ticked here: AC-091.**
  - **Stage 5, 2026-09-23: the keyboard (AC-100), which completes AC-094.**
    - A tile is a tab stop in view mode as well, and answers the marking's keys there: arrows move between its items, Space marks the focused one, Ctrl and Space toggle it, Shift and an arrow extend from the anchor, and Escape unmarks the tile's marking. The same tab stop as edit mode, a different vocabulary, because arranging and reading are different things to be doing — and the tile's accessible name says which keys it answers.
    - **Arrows do not mark.** Every marking change re-queries each tile using it, so "select as you move" would fire a round of queries per keystroke; the move is announced instead ("shipped, 2 of 3. Space marks."), since nothing on screen says where the keyboard is.
    - An extend goes through `addItemsWithinLimit`, so a long Shift-extend stops at the 1,000-item cap and says so rather than refusing the gesture.
    - **Tests:** `e2e/markings.spec.ts` drives a focused tile with the keyboard alone — arrow announcing without marking, Space marking, Shift extending, Ctrl+Space toggling back, Escape unmarking.
    - **Ticked here: AC-100, and AC-094**, whose empty-plot-area half landed in stage 1.
  - **Stage 6, 2026-09-23: a tile that cannot reach the marking (AC-103).**
    - Such a tile is left unmarked and says so, rather than drawing every item faded — which would read as "none of it is in here", a different and wrong answer — and rather than sending a query Cube would refuse.
    - **This needed the model to be decisive, and it was not.** `reachFrom` only ruled a pair out when their join components differed, and a cube with no joins reports no component at all, so the answer was "cannot say" and nothing was labelled. Verified against the local Cube v1.7.42: `orders`, `products` and `customers` report `connectedComponent: 1`; `monthly_orders`, which declares no joins, reports none. `markings-query-support.md` §4.5 had this as a source reading marked UNVERIFIED; it is now verified there, with the probe.
    - **Absence counts only where the model reports components at all.** A model that says nothing about them — a different Cube version, or one read before the joins compiled — is telling us nothing, and reading that as "every cube is isolated" would stop every filter reaching every tile. That case stays "cannot say", and has its own test.
    - The same rule now spares dashboard filters a doomed query too (AC-079): a tile that cannot be reached is marked as such before anything is sent.
    - **Tests:** `filters/coverage.test.ts` (a join-less cube ruled out, its own members still its own, a joined pair unaffected, and silence everywhere still "cannot say") and `e2e/markings.spec.ts` — a tile on `monthly_orders` labelled not linked, unmarked, nothing faded, and no error on it.
    - **Ticked here: AC-103.**
  - **Stage 7, 2026-09-25: marking with a rectangle or a lasso (AC-088, AC-089).**
    - **Gestures.** A drag on a tile that marks draws a dashed rectangle over the chart. With Alt it draws a lasso. On release, it marks every item the shape touched.
      - The overlay is SVG over the canvas, drawn by `ChartCanvas`, as the prototype draws it.
      - `dragGesture` decides drag from click on the same 5 px as `itemClicks`, so exactly one of them answers any press.
      - A drag's release never counts as a click on empty plot area, which would unmark the tile.
    - **What a shape touches.** `itemsInShape` (`charts/src/interaction`) reads the chart as drawn through `convertToPixel`, which is what `research/echarts.md` says marking must rest on.
      - Bars, stacked segments, horizontal bars, line points, scatter points and heatmap cells are covered.
      - Each item is named as a click names it, so the dashboard reads a drag and a click through the same `clickedValue`.
      - Pies and treemaps have no axis to convert along. They mark by click, as the prototype's do.
    - **What it does to the marking** (`onMarkShape`):
      - A plain drag replaces the marking.
      - Ctrl or ⌘ toggles the enclosed items when all or none are marked, and otherwise adds them. This is `applyToggleOrAdd`'s rule, and a tile marked whole is expanded first, as a Ctrl-click expands it.
      - Growth stops at the 1,000-item cap and says so (`addItemsWithinLimit`).
      - A shape that touched nothing changes nothing, as in the prototype.
    - **Found on the way, fixed.** `touchesSpan` sampled nine points along a bar. A thin rectangle across a tall bar's foot fell between two samples and missed it: the e2e's first drag did exactly that. It is now exact: an end inside the shape, or the span crossing one of the shape's edges. The sampling test became one of a 1-pixel strip across a 1,000-pixel bar, for both a rectangle and a lasso.
    - **Tests:**
      - `charts/src/interaction/itemsInShape.test.ts`: a bar crossed at its foot, a miss, a lasso, a stacked segment, a horizontal bar, a line's and a scatter's points, the category an item carries, a gap.
      - `e2e/markings.spec.ts` "marking with a shape", on a real dashboard in all three browsers:
        - a rectangle over two bars marks both;
        - an Alt-lasso round the third replaces them;
        - a press moved under 5 px is a click;
        - Ctrl-dragging over a partly marked pair adds, over an unmarked bar toggles it on, and over the wholly marked pair toggles them off.
      - All failed first, for want of the drag.
    - **Ticked here: AC-088, AC-089.**
    - **Review 2026-09-25 (cold, FAIL), fixed once:**
      - **Log axes.** A shape on a log value axis marked every bar: its base was 0, whose pixel is infinite. A bar now starts at 1 there, as ECharts' does, and an item whose pixels are not finite is not marked.
      - **Bars are hit as the rectangles ECharts draws**, not their centre line. Each column's slot in the band follows ECharts' own layout (`laidBarWidth`, `research/echarts-bar-density.md`): unstacked series a column each, a stack one, and overlaid bars one. So a grouped bar is found by its own slot, and a wide bar by its edge. `hitTest.touchesRect` is exact, as `touchesSpan` is.
      - **Mixed-sign stacks** stack by sign, as ECharts 6.1 does (`samesign`). A negative segment is found below the baseline.
      - **A drag is never also a click.** An out-and-back drag ending on its bar, or a drag along a trellis header, fired both. The series and header releases now defer to a drag under way, and a header press is told apart by where it happened. `itemClicks.cancel` was added, and `itemClick.test.ts` covers it.
      - **Only the primary button marks.** zrender reports every button alike, so a right-click marked the item under it, or unmarked from empty plot area. A context menu opening cancels any press under way. That includes macOS's Ctrl+click, which presses the primary button (`research/context-menu-and-submenus.md`).
        - So on a Mac, toggling is ⌘ (AC-087 and AC-089 name both keys).
        - The e2e now presses `ControlOrMeta`, which is ⌘ on a Mac. Before, it pressed Control, the Mac's context-menu gesture. On Windows and Linux it is Ctrl, as before.
      - **A release belongs to the tile it was pressed on.** A drag overshooting onto a neighbouring tile no longer clears that tile's marking.
      - **A lost release ends the drag.** One that never arrives (another window, a context menu, the window losing focus) ends the drag with nothing marked, and a release of another button mid-drag is ignored.
      - **No rubber band** on a pie, donut, treemap, KPI, table or pivot, a tile set to "(None)", or a tile that can't reach its marking.
      - **A plain drag over nothing** replaces the marking with nothing, as direction.md rule 47 has it, like a click on empty plot area. With Ctrl or ⌘ it adds nothing.
      - **The tooltip** is hidden on every move of a drag, not only the first.
      - **Tests added:**
        - `itemsInShape.test.ts`: a bar's edge, a grouped bar's slot and the gap beside it, a mixed-sign stack, a log axis. All four failed first.
        - `e2e/markings.spec.ts` "a drag out and back, a right-click, an overshoot and an empty drag each do one thing", in all three browsers.
      - **Also fixed:** the AC-106 test's doc comment, which stage 7's block had separated from its test.
      - **Left as is:** a heatmap cell marks its column, as a click on it does (older than this stage). The part of a bar clipped off the plot when the axis leaves out zero can still be hit.
      - **A slip in T119's commit:** its new menu items broke "a chart tile's menu offers…". I had run only T119's own test before committing. The list is updated here, and the whole markings suite (102 tests) passes.
  - **Stage 8, 2026-09-25: the 1,000-item cap on a real tile (AC-102).**
    - T108 built the rule. It was ticked on `limit.test.ts` on 2026-09-20 and has been shown on a tile only now.
    - `e2e/markings.spec.ts` "a shape over more than 1,000 items…" uses a cube of the browser's own over `generate_series(1, 1500)`, drawn as a 1,500-bar tile (a bar chart folds categories only when its Top N is set).
      - A rectangle across the whole plot marks 1,000, and the announcement says "A marking holds at most 1,000 items. 500 were not added."
      - Mark all then marks all 1,500, because it stores the tile's filter.
    - **Found on the way, fixed:** the badge and the announcement printed "1000" beside a limit written "1,000". Both now group thousands (`en-GB`), as the chip and the limit message already did. Unit tests were added to `MarkBadge.test.tsx` and `LiveRegion.test.tsx`; both failed first.
    - **Ticked here: AC-102.** It was ticked on T108's unit test, then withdrawn with the other seventeen on 2026-09-20.
  - **Why this task exists.** T086–T119 each built and tested one module, and every one of their Files lists names only that module and its test — no renderer, no e2e spec. The F5–F9 dashboard tasks by contrast each list `DashboardView.tsx` and `e2e/dashboard.spec.ts`. So the plan never contained the step that makes marking reachable, and 18 criteria were ticked on unit tests of code nothing imports. Unticked 2026-09-20; see the status note in `docs/spec.md` under F10.
  - **The lesson worth keeping, independent of markings.** A criterion whose `Fails when:` names an observation on a tile is not demonstrated by a test that renders a component with hand-passed props. When planning any future feature, the task that introduces a UI module must also name the renderer that mounts it, or the feature is finished everywhere except where the user is.
  - Known interface hazard for whoever does this: `allLimitsEmpty(limitingMarkings(xs))` is false for every input, because `limitingMarkings` keeps only the non-empty markings. Pinned by a test in `NothingMarked.test.tsx`.

## Spec F22. Following the design prototype's structure

Planned 2026-09-24 from the critiques in `docs/design/critiques/2026-09-24-*.md` (R9: the user chose to do this before more features, then resume the handoff order). Every task here is surface work, so every one names the renderer and an e2e spec — the lesson of T190 above. The prototype is served for comparison with `python3 -m http.server 5500` in `docs/design/prototype/`.

Order: the reopened criteria first (they are ticked-and-false, the worst state to leave), then Explore and the shell, then dashboards.

- [x] T208 (AC-042) Offer Retry and details on a dashboard tile's error state, and never report a failed query as a missing chart
  - Files: `packages/web/src/dashboard/DashboardView.tsx`, `packages/web/src/dashboard/DashboardPage.tsx`, `packages/web/src/dashboard/chartSpec.ts`, `packages/web/src/query/loadTile.ts`, `e2e/dashboard.spec.ts`
  - Failing test: `e2e/dashboard.spec.ts`: a tile whose query fails shows its title, Retry and a details disclosure; Retry asks again and draws the chart (AC-042).
  - Depends on: none
  - Done 2026-09-24. AC-042 re-ticked on four e2e tests in `e2e/dashboard.spec.ts`, all passing in Chrome, Firefox and WebKit: the chart-shaped skeleton while queries are held; a 500 from Cube giving the title, the message, Show query and a Retry that draws the chart; a dropped network during a refresh giving a retryable error rather than "no longer available", and Retry recovering it; and a 404 giving the missing-chart state with no Retry.
  - **Two causes, both found by reading what the critique saw.** `TileBody` rendered `<TileError error={error} />` and never passed `onRetry` — the component test passed the prop, so it was green while no dashboard ever showed the button. And `specFor` caught *every* failure to fetch the chart document as "This chart is no longer available", so a dropped network read as a deleted chart. It now separates a 404 (missing) from a network failure or other HTTP status (a failed load).
  - **The cold review found four more, all fixed.** The title vanished in the error state, which the task itself required — the tile now keeps its heading. A deleted chart received a Retry that could only fail — `CHART_MISSING` is now one shared value and the tile renders the missing state for it, with no Retry, as it does for `CHART_UNTYPED`. A network failure at `/api/load` was a bare `TypeError` with nothing behind "details" — `loadTile` now wraps it in a `TileLoadError` carrying the query, leaving a cancellation a cancellation. And Retry showed in edit mode, where Refresh is hidden because a drafted tile's re-read would drop the draft.
  - **Recorded, not fixed:** a 200 response whose body will not parse is reported as "could not reach the server". A wrong message, not a wrong state; left for the next time `getJson` is touched.

  - Failing test: `e2e/dashboard.spec.ts`: the Outline lists page tabs, then their items with sections and tab groups nested, and clicking a row selects that element (AC-053).
  - Depends on: none
  - Done 2026-09-24. AC-053 re-ticked on `e2e/dashboard.spec.ts` "the Outline shows the dashboard as a tree, and a row selects its element", in Chrome, Firefox and WebKit. It names every element of the seeded dashboard in order, by chart title or text; checks a section's chart is inside the section's item; and selects an element further down (and brings it into view), one on the page tab that is not open, and one in a tab group's tab that is not showing.
  - **The cold review found three real problems, all fixed.** A row in a tab group's hidden tab selected an element with no box on the canvas — the tab group kept its open tab to itself — so it now follows a selection into the tab that holds it, once per new selection so a hand switch still works. The first version used ARIA tree roles without the tree's keyboard pattern, which promises arrow keys and expansion to exactly the people who rely on them; it is now nested lists of buttons, whose depth is announced and which promise nothing extra. And the test checked names by regex with `.first()`, not scrolling, and not the hidden tab; it checks all three now.

  - Depends on: none
  - Done 2026-09-24. AC-005 and AC-211 ticked on `e2e/a11y-tokens.spec.ts`, all three browsers: every chart's SVG text on the seeded dashboard meets 4.5:1 against the tile it sits on in dark (composited for alpha and opacity, and only once every chart has drawn); a bar's slot-*n* light colour becomes exactly slot *n* of the dark ramp on switching the theme, without a reload; a pie, a heatmap and a trellis in dark draw no light categorical colour and no text under AA; the open palette's results pass axe in both themes; Security's dashboard links pass in dark.
  - **Why the audit missed it:** axe's colour-contrast rule does not measure text inside an SVG, and the palette was audited closed. Chart text is now measured directly, by `CHART_TEXT_CONTRAST`.
  - **`themed(option, theme)`** is applied last, in `ChartCanvas` — the one place every ECharts surface goes through — so no renderer has to know the theme. Categorical colours swap slot for slot, so a member keeps its place in the order (AC-039); "Other" takes direction.md's dark neutral; text, lines and the tooltip take the tokens. The light theme takes its own tokens too, rather than ECharts' defaults.
  - **The sequential ramp is reversed in dark, not recoloured.** direction.md publishes one ramp, light to dark, whose high end sank into the dark tile at about 1.4:1. Its two published ends the other way round keep the ramp's rule — magnitude reads as contrast against the surface — with no colour invented. A decision taken here, recorded so it can be overturned; a dark ramp of its own would be direction.md's to publish.
  - **The cold review found five real problems, all fixed.** The global link rule `a:visited` outranked a Primary link tile's own colour and would have drawn its text in accent on its accent fill — now `:where()`, with no specificity. Gridlines a user turns on kept a hard-coded light colour, and "Other" its light grey. Tooltips were ECharts' white box. And the recolouring swapped *any* string equal to a palette hex, so a data value that was a colour would have been renamed on the axis and in the name a click marks by — it now touches only colour keys. The e2e also got stronger: the exact dark slot, alpha and opacity, every chart rather than the first, and chart types beyond bars.

- [x] T254 (AC-187) Draw a chart's text in Inter with tabular numerals, and its plot down to the tile's foot, as the prototype does
  - Files: `packages/charts/src/{themed,optionFor}.ts` (+ tests), `packages/charts/src/layout/grid.ts`, `packages/charts/src/series/{bar,combo}.ts`, `packages/web/src/tiles/ChartCanvas.tsx`, `packages/web/src/shell/styles.ts`, `docs/research/echarts-text-and-grid.md`, `docs/research/echarts-bar-density.md`, `e2e/design-conformance.spec.ts`, `e2e/{markings,crossfilter}.spec.ts`
  - Failing test: `e2e/design-conformance.spec.ts` "T254: …": every SVG text is Inter, with tabular numerals; the lowest label is no more than 12 px above the chart's foot (the prototype's `grid: { bottom: 8, containLabel: true }`) (recheck-dashboard N7, F9; mismatches 12, 13).
  - Depends on: `docs/research/echarts-text-and-grid.md` (ECharts 6.1's global `textStyle`, how its SVG writes text, and v6's grid label bounds)
  - Done 2026-09-24, all three browsers. The e2e failed first, and so did `themed.test.ts` "a chart's text" and `optionFor.test.ts` "a chart on axes".
    - **The chart's text is Inter.** It is set through the option's root `textStyle`, which reaches every text wechart draws; ECharts writes the family inline, so page CSS can't. The tooltip is the prototype's 12 px.
    - **Tabular numerals come from page CSS on the chart**, as ECharts has no option for them. Most of its text inherits them. The few written with the `font` shorthand get them through an `!important` rule, and the tooltip through its `extraCssText`.
    - **One limit, recorded in the research:** zrender measures text with a canvas, which has no tabular figures. The labels are laid out by proportional digit widths and drawn tabular. How far the two differ for Inter at 12 px is UNVERIFIED.
    - **The grid is the prototype's `{ left: 8, right: 28, top: 12, bottom: 8 }`**, in ECharts 6's supported terms: `outerBoundsMode: 'same'` with `outerBoundsContain: 'all'`. Axis titles stay inside the 8 px bottom too. `containLabel` is deprecated, and wechart's build doesn't register the legacy algorithm the prototype's full bundle ran. The legend's room and the Customize tab's placement still win.
    - **Bars and combos carry the grid themselves**, so a bar's estimated width is measured against the grid it is drawn on: `width − 36` along it, `height − 20` down a horizontal chart. `echarts-bar-density.md` says so.
    - **Found by the full run:**
      - The markings and cross-filter e2e helpers clicked a bar at Playwright's `boundingBox()` of its axis label.
      - In WebKit that box sits half the label's width to the right for middle-anchored SVG text. With the wider plot, the click fell in the gap between two bars.
      - Both helpers now measure with the element's own client rect, and wait for it to settle. The measurement is recorded in `docs/research/playwright-webkit-svg-text-box.md`.
  - **The cold review failed it on AC-210, fixed:**
    - **The bar-width estimate** took only the grid's edges. It kept the gap on bars really under 4 px, which drew them empty, with a legend at the bottom or wide currency ticks in a narrow tile. It now subtracts the legend's room where one is drawn (`plotEdgesOf`) and a value-label allowance, erring under. Both cases are drawn through `optionFor` in `bar.test.ts`, and fail without the fix.
    - **Hiding or moving the legend** had put the plot's top back at ECharts' default 65 px. Customize now keeps the prototype's 12 (tested in `optionFor.test.ts`), and the grid test asserts 12 rather than "a number".
    - **Also:**
      - the tooltip's `extraCssText` is joined with a separator;
      - the cross-filter helper waits for a settled box too;
      - the unsourced claim about Inter's digits is marked UNVERIFIED.
    - **Recorded choice:** the grid keeps ECharts' default 25 % clamp, not the research's 0. Very long labels then overflow, rather than shrinking the plot to nothing, which would itself draw empty axes. `nameMoveOverlap` stays at its default, which keeps axis titles clear of the labels and, under `'all'`, inside the grid.

- [x] T266 (AC-199, AC-246) Make the tile menu a menu with submenus, opened by ⋯, a right-click on the plot, Shift+F10 and the Menu key
  - Done 2026-09-25, all three browsers. AC-246 ticked on `e2e/markings.spec.ts` "a right-click on the chart, Shift+F10 or the Menu key opens the tile's menu, and marks nothing". It failed first, as did `shell/Menu.test.tsx`. AC-199 waits for T272's Export.
    - **`shell/Menu`** is the WAI-ARIA APG Menu pattern (research/context-menu-and-submenus.md), one implementation for every opener:
      - items, checkbox items, submenus, named groups and separators;
      - ↓ ↑ wrap, Home and End;
      - Enter runs an item and closes, and so does Space except on a checkbox item, which it toggles while the menu stays open;
      - → Enter or Space opens a submenu on its first item, and ← or Escape closes only that submenu;
      - Escape at the top closes the menu, and Tab from anywhere closes all of it.
      - Items are elements with roles, not buttons, so Space and Enter can differ on a checkbox item (the research's gotcha 10).
      - A disabled item stays focusable, and its reason is its description (`aria-describedby`), which a keyboard reaches where a tooltip did not (T182).
    - **The view-mode tile menu** is that menu:
      - Its marked group's heading sits outside the menu, which holds items only, and names the group.
      - It opens in the top layer (`popover="manual"`), so a right-click puts it at the pointer, clear of the tile's box. It is turned back from the window's edges, and when opened from ⋯ it is kept inside the dashboard canvas, as T253's review asked.
    - **The openers:**
      - ⋯, as before.
      - A right-click on the chart opens the menu at the pointer, the browser's menu is prevented, and the press it began marks nothing (T190's cancel on `contextmenu`).
      - Shift+F10 or the Menu key on a focused chart tile opens it at the tile, in every view mode. Chart tiles are now tab stops in cross-filter mode too, and their spoken keys say "Shift and F10 open its menu". Escape then gives focus back to the tile.
    - **Tests updated one for one:** the tile menu's `list` and `button` roles became `menu` and `menuitem`, and a disabled item's `.disabled` became `aria-disabled`.
      - `TileViewMenu.test.tsx`: the test-integrity hook flags this as "replaces a strict matcher with a weaker one". It is a false positive: the renamed line was `toBeTruthy` before too, and `toBe(true)` on `.disabled` became `toBe('true')` on `aria-disabled`. Reported to the user.
      - The design checks measure the popup the menu sits in (`viewMenuOf`).
      - T119's disabled-reason check reads the accessible description instead of `title`.
  - **T266's review, 2026-09-25.** One cold review, which judged AC-246 met only in part. Everything it found is fixed in one commit, all three browsers:
    - **H1. A keyboard's `contextmenu` opened the browser's menu.** Only the plot prevented `contextmenu`. On Windows, Chromium fires the Menu key's on keyup, at the item the menu has just focused, so the browser's menu opened over ours. VoiceOver's VO+Shift+M fires one at the focused tile. Now:
      - the popup prevents every `contextmenu` inside it;
      - a `contextmenu` on the focused chart tile itself opens its menu (`Canvas`'s new `onTileContextMenu`) and prevents the browser's.
      - The e2e dispatches both events where a browser would, since Playwright makes none from a key (research §7), and checks that each key's keydown default is prevented. **AC-246 stays ticked on that test**, which now observes this path.
    - **M1. Submenus would have been clipped** by the popup's `overflow: auto`. A submenu is now `position: fixed`, placed from its item's box and turned back from the window's edges (research §6). This was latent until T270–T273 add submenus. `Menu.test.tsx` checks the placement.
    - **M2. A macOS Ctrl+click could unmark a tile.** The `contextmenu` cancelled the chart's presses but not the wrapper's, so a release off the menu read as a click on empty plot. It now ends that press too. **No test:** the reviewer did not reproduce it, and Playwright cannot place the release off a flipped menu without depending on the window size. The change is the one line the finding names.
    - **L1.** A submenu inside a group can now be reached. `OWN_ITEMS` includes `group > none > menuitem`, with a test.
    - **L2.** A press on the popup's heading or padding keeps focus on the item it was on, so Escape still closes the menu. Before, focus went to the tile, and Escape unmarked it with the menu still open.
    - **L4.** In view mode outside Markings, only chart tiles are tab stops (`Canvas`'s new `takesKeys`). A text or image tile answers no key there. `Canvas.test.tsx` checks this; it was written after the code.
    - **L3 (no change):** a right-click on a KPI, table or pivot keeps the browser's menu. AC-246 names the plot, and a table's text is worth copying.
    - **L5:** covered by the e2e additions above.

Added 2026-09-25 by the UI review stream. Its sources:

- the T225 re-critique of every surface (`docs/design/critiques/2026-09-25-*.md`);
- T182's cold review.

Only gaps that break an accepted criterion or a numbered direction.md rule are tasks here. The rest are proposed spec changes for the user, not built.

    - e2e: on a dashboard, a bar split by status and a donut of status draw each status in the same colour (AC-039).

    - **`colouredMembersOf(spec)`**, new in `@wechart/charts` (`colouredMembers.ts`), names what a chart colours:
