# Phase 2

Inputs: `docs/spec.md` F25–F36 and the phase-1 criteria returned or rewritten for phase 2 (104 open criteria); `docs/requirements.md` Part 2 (R11–R23); `docs/research/` (openid-client, dex, credential-encryption, cube/per-folder-models, connection-testing, box-plot, country-map, scheduler, and the CodeMirror merge research); `docs/design/direction.md` §7e and rules 59–89.

The `[moved to phase 2]` tasks above are superseded by the tasks below, which carry their notes forward where they still hold.

**Amended 2026-09-26** by the final integration plan (`docs/inputs/2026-09-26-integration-plan-decisions.md`, cited `[IP n]`; its doc's snapshot `docs/inputs/2026-09-26-integration-plan.md`, cited `[plan]`), round R28, and the spec's amendment (AC-319 to AC-332).
- Tasks the plan overturns are retired or rewritten in place, with the old text struck through and the ID kept.
- wechart's side of the plan's slices 2–8 is in **P2.17**, one task per behaviour. Each waits on xcube's routes for its slice. Those are built on the Cube side, never from this repository.
- All work is on branch `feat/xcube` until the user merges it (R28 Q10).
- New research: `cube/xcube-runtime.md`, `cube/prefixed-names.md`, `cube/generated-policies.md`, `cube/whole-model-publish.md`, `cube/tokens-and-service-credential.md` (`jose` 6.2.12), `cube/ha-topology.md`, `credential-sealing.md` (`hpke` 1.1.7) and `cube/xcube-rename.md`, each marked where the plan supersedes it.

**Decisions this plan takes** (small, under the standing instruction; each can be changed with its task):

- **Where the user comes from.** Every request carries `request.wechartUser = { key, name, groups, superAdmin }`. With security off it is the one user `admin`, a Super-Admin. With security on it comes from the server-side session. Handlers read nothing else (research `openid-client.md`, "Security off").
- **Group access is stored on the folder.** Each folder document's body gains `access: { readOnly: string[] | null, readWrite: string[] | null }`, where `null` means unset. The shared root's access is a `setting` document `root-access`. Effective access is computed in memory from the folder list by a pure function in `packages/core/src/access/`.
- **Workspaces are folder ids** of the form `ws:<userKey>`. The phase-1 pseudo-root `mine` resolves to the signed-in user's workspace, and phase-1 items in `mine` move to the workspace of the single user `admin`.
- ~~**The folder chain Cube compiles** is the list of model-bearing folder ids, nearest first, in a signed `wechartModel` claim that only the API mints after checking access (research `cube/per-folder-models.md`, layout B).~~ **Superseded 2026-09-25** by the user's architecture decisions 1–3 and 5 (`docs/inputs/2026-09-25-architecture-decisions.md`; requirements §P2.4 "Architecture", R27). Cube plus xcube serve one flat model under folder-id prefixes. xcube binds short names at publish, nearest first from each item's own folder. No chain is signed into tokens. **Then, 2026-09-26** `[IP 1–4]`: wechart publishes changesets and the folder tree to xcube, and xcube compiles the published items as modules.
- **The security-on end-to-end suite is separate.** It is `playwright.security.config.ts`, with its own API (port 4300), web preview (port 5373) and Dex, so the phase-1 suite (security off) stays as it is until AC-308's end-of-phase check (the user's R13).
- **Every API route declares its access class**: `public` (health and `/api/auth/*`), `cube` (key-guarded model routes), `user`, or `admin` (a Super-Admin's alone, T323). A test fails for any unclassified route (T318). *The `cube` class goes with the model routes (decision 1: Cube never calls wechart; AC-251, AC-327). That happens in ~~slice 3~~ slice 2's cut-over (T431, done 2026-09-26).*
- **The service credential and xcube's admin routes (2026-09-26).** wechart calls xcube's admin API (`/v1/semantic/*`, `[plan]` "The contract") only from its server, with a service token of its own (`role: service`, `aud: xcube-admin`). The contract's paths are the plan's draft. A route the tasks need but the draft lacks, such as the JWKS push, is proposed on the plan doc's contract section before it is built.

      - isn't a JWK;
      - holds a private part (`d`);
      - isn't X25519;
      - has an `x` that isn't 32 bytes of canonical base64url;
      - has a `kid` other than its thumbprint;
      - is a point no key can be agreed with.

      - an item the user may not open answers 404, as a missing one does. Opening follows `itemFor`: a reader opens the charts on their dashboards. A proposal opens for its author, the read-write members of every folder it lands in, and the Super-Admins, as its route has it;
      - a query naming a cube or view its item isn't bound to answers 403. That covers its measures, dimensions, segments, time dimensions, filters (nested `and` and `or` too) and order.
      - An item is bound to the cubes it uses and those they join through. For a published item those are its own cubes (bound at publish, so its body is trusted) and the cubes on its folder's path, since a drill asks a tile's joined cubes (AC-236, AC-237) and they bind along that path. The same goes for each chart a dashboard shows, from wherever it is kept.
      - A workspace item's body is its author's to write and bound to nothing, so it reaches only the cubes on the shared root's path and its target folder's (AC-329). A proposal likewise reaches the paths of the folders it lands in, and the published charts a proposed dashboard shows. Paths are read from the model files, not asked of Cube.
      - Workspace items are answered from the published model until T347's overlays.
      - A query that isn't one object, or names a member by anything but a name, answers 400. Join hints are read with the rest.
      - A chart this wechart can't read (a newer format) is left out of its dashboard's reach rather than failing every tile.
    - **A query naming no item** answers 400, but a Super-Admin's, who may open every item (a small decision, reported). The security suite's own API calls as `super`, and the Security page's generated SQL (Super-Admins only with sign-in on), name none.
    - **`/api/meta?for=`** answers the item's cubes and views alone. Asked for none, it is the user's groups' field list, as before. The web app doesn't ask it per item yet (for T408's route matrix to judge).
    - **A preview** (T172) is refused a non-Super-Admin before the item is checked, as before.
    - **The web app** names the item in every query:
      - `QueryItemContext` (`query/item.ts`), set by `DashboardView` (the dashboard, or the proposal a review draws it from) and by the chart editor's route (the chart);
      - `loadTile`'s `item`; `specFor` and `drawChartBody`;
      - FilterBar, FilteredCharts, LiveToken, ViewQuery, ChartEditor, Wells, ResultsDrawer, AccelerationPanel, ChartEditorOverlay (the dashboard it is edited on), the chart page's save, `ReadOnlyDashboard` (history, reviews) and the review view.
    - **Tests changed, not weakened:** `auth/cube-groups.test.ts`'s route tests name a dashboard in the root that uses `orders` (with sign-in on they would answer 400). `web/dashboard/refreshTile.test.tsx`'s exact body now carries `for`. `e2e/security/cube-groups.spec.ts` gives its users a dashboard on the secured view to ask for.

- [x] T372 [P] (AC-150) Record each build wechart starts, one record per start, and follow it to its end on the server
  - *Rewritten 2026-10-02 to design 16 (`[R56]`):* one record per start (Q6), its four outcomes, and starters that include wechart's schedules.
  - **As built (2026-10-02):**
    - Migration `1758530000000_build-history.cjs`: `build_runs`, one row per start (pre-aggregation, folder, partitions asked, partition granularity, how it was started, a person or a schedule as starter, request id, when wechart asked and when Cube answered, end, outcome, failed count, Cube's error), and `build_tokens`, one row per job (last state, table, end, a jsonb log of each state with when wechart saw it, and a lease).
    - `repos/build-history.ts`; `jobs/follow.ts`, started by `main.ts` every 2 s and stopped with the process; `POST /api/builds` sends `x-request-id: wechart-<uuid>` and answers the record's `runId`.
    - **Following across replicas:** a follower takes open jobs on a 30 s lease (an `UPDATE … WHERE` the lease has run out, which a concurrent taker re-checks and passes by, research `db-access.md` §3), least lately asked first, asks Cube, writes each new state only if the job still holds the state it was taken in, and hands the jobs back to be asked again a second on, only if it still holds them. Each round also closes every open build whose jobs have all ended.
    - **The first moments:** within 30 s of Cube's answer to the post, `not_found` and `missing_partition` aren't taken as a job's end (research `cube/job-records.md`, "Statuses that can flip…", an inference). After that, a state seen again and now taken as the end keeps the time it was first seen. The 30 s is the implementer's call that research leaves open.
    - **Outcomes:** failed when any job failed (`failure: …`, `missing_partition`, `pre_agg_not_found`), its error the first `failure: …` text; else Cube's record expired when any job read `not_found`, with no end or duration, since how it ended isn't known; else done.
    - **Not recorded:** a start for which Cube made no job (the browser is told no job started, as before). The pre-aggregation's folder is found before Cube is asked, so a failure there starts nothing.
    - A batch Cube refuses is asked again job by job, so one job whose context no longer compiles holds up no other.
    - The cap: each start locks its pre-aggregation's oldest record first, so two starts at once trim in turn.
  - **One review round (spec-reviewer), fixed:** a build never closed when a round stopped between a job's end and its build's close; the folder read after the post; tokens past the first 100 never asked; the cap racing two starts; a start with no job recorded as Done; one bad job failing its batch; the first moments counted from before the post; an expired build given an end and a duration; a status kept as Cube's error; a late follower handing back another's hold. Tests added for each, and for `startFollowingBuilds`.

      - `readCron`: five fields, each in range, read back in words, or refused naming the field. It also says whether a refresh key could run it, by core's `refreshEveryRefusal`. pg-boss's own check is the last word.
      - `nextRunsOf`: the next runs from pg-boss's `previewSchedule`, with the first clock change among them and how many runs come before it. Core's `clockChangeBetween` finds the change; it's split out of `nextRefreshesBeforeChange`.

    - **The count isn't stored. It is read from Run history** (`scheduler/suspend.ts`, `failuresOf`):
      - it reads the schedule's latest runs that ended done or failed, started after `counted_from`, newest first, at most its number, and counts the failed ones in a row;

      - after a refused start;

    - **Resume** (`POST /api/wechart-schedules/:id/resume`, scoped as a change is, in the route matrix):
      - clears the suspension and sets `counted_from` to now, so the count starts again from 0;
      - lays pg-boss's schedule anew, so it runs from its next time, with nothing missed while it was suspended;
      - names who resumed it as its last changer.

A chart with none asks nothing new, so its query and its cache entry stay as they were. A box plot asks none: its rows are each one observation.
    - **Read back.** xcube answers each calculation in its companion's column, `<measure>__xc_<calculation>`, a suffix no authored member may hold. `loadTile` reads that column, and its annotation, back under the measure's name. The value is Cube's, as it came; nothing is worked out in the browser.
    - **A running total from the chart's range.** xcube filters on the range of the query's time field at its grain, so a dashboard's date filter on the chart's own time field starts the total there: March 31, April 61 (e2e). So `loadTile` asks them apart, each as any query is, with its own request id to cancel, and joins their rows by the rest of their columns. A period missing from one keeps the other's value. The data are as old as the oldest part, and served from rollups only where both were. View query asks each part for its SQL.
    - **Named.** `compile` gives each calculated measure a `calculated` entry. Its title and short title gain the calculation, in xcube's words: "Count (running total)", "(difference from previous month)", "(3-month moving average)". `withMemberLabels` is what every place uses to put the model's titles and formats on a drawn chart: the dashboard's tiles and drills, the chart page and the review view. So the label survives the model's titles arriving later.
    - **Written.** A share (% of total, % difference) is written as a percentage, and a rank as a plain number.   - **Done 2026-10-04**, with R63 (the user: "The member who took it up").
    - **What resolves a request.** An approved proposal resolves an open request when two things hold:
      - its author took the request up, by opening it in their workspace (T384);
      - one of the model files it lands, in the request's folder, adds a measure to the request's cube. A measure is added when the file it replaced didn't have it (a new file adds every measure).
      
      The request names those measures, by full name, with the proposal's author, its approver and when. A measure added by anyone who hasn't opened the request leaves it open, and so does a taker's proposal that adds nothing to its cube. Resolved once: a later approval changes nothing.
    - **Where.** After an approval has landed its models and settled (`afterModelsLanded`, given each file as it landed and as it was), the open requests of those folders are read with their takers (`openOn`) and resolved (`resolve`). A failure there is logged and never undoes the approval.
    - **Shown.** `GET /api/calc-requests` gives each request its `resolution`: `{ members, by, approvedBy, at }`, or null. The Reviews list says "Resolved". The summary says "Resolved by <cube.measure>, … · added by <author>, approved by <approver> · <when>", with the ok icon and no live region, and offers no opening. The pane beside the model editor says the same, in place of what to do next.

  - **Done 2026-09-30.**
    - Files, as built:
      - `packages/api/src/access/route-matrix.test.ts`;
      - `server.ts` (the image and `…/queries/find` routes; introspection's `seesSource`);
      - `model/introspection.ts`, `repos/images.ts`, `repos/query-log.ts` (+ test);

    - **The matrix.** Its world:
      - /A (read-only `sales-ro`), /A/B (read-write `sales-rw`), /A/B/C (read-only `g20`) and /C (read-write `managers`), and the shared root, which no group is granted.
      - Each of the five places holds a dashboard with a chart of its own and an image, a library chart, a model file with a rollup, a data source, and a kept version.
      - A root library chart is shown on /A/B's and /C's dashboards.
      - `writer` and `manager` each have a workspace dashboard and chart, a proposal, a bookmark and a query in the log.
      - Six users sign in through Dex: `super`, `writer`, `reader`, `many` (20 groups), `manager` and `nobody`.
      - Each item is a secret: its ids, its title, and marks written into it (an image's bytes, a model's comment, a version's description, Cube's rows).
      - Each secret names who may see it. The rights table spells out AC-261, AC-262, AC-263, AC-255 and AC-265, rather than calling `folderRights`.
    - **The checks.**
      - Every answer, whatever its status, is searched for every secret its user may not see.
      - Each case also checks the answer itself: what the user may open answers with its mark, and anything else is refused (401, 403 or 404).
      - A change is made by those who may make it, and refused to everyone else with the item unchanged. The no-op changes (a save or rename to the same) keep the world as it was.
      - A shared dashboard's save is 409 `shared_in_place` even for its writers (T502).
      - Lists and search show what the user may see, so no case is empty. Counts in the tree are exact (AC-194).
      - A query refused for its item never reaches Cube (T340).
      - The first test reads every route from the server (`routesOf`; a HEAD is its GET's) and fails for a route with no case, or a case with no route: 83 routes.
    - **The stub Cube answers as xcube's gate does** (AC-320). Each place's cube is admitted to the groups its folder allows. A route that asked Cube as anyone but its user would bring back another place's cube titles or rows.
    - **Found and fixed.** Seven routes, in three places, gave out what their user may not see:
      - `GET /api/images/:id` answered anyone with the id. An image now goes to one who may open a stored dashboard showing it: the one it was added to, or any other, such as one an approval landed it on (the catalog's `dashboardsShowingImage`).
        - That trusts a stored body, so a save now puts on a dashboard only images its user may see, or that it already showed (`addsOnlyReadableImages`, 403). This covers `PUT /api/documents/dashboard/:id` and `PUT /api/dashboards/:id`.
        - An import leaves behind an image the importer may not see: its tile shows none (`keepsImage`, as `keepsChart` does for charts).
        - Copies, restores, proposals and approvals write only what the user could already open.
        - Named by the tile asking for it (`?for=dashboard:<id>` or `proposal:<id>`, as a query names its item), an image is also shown in two more cases: when a kept version of that dashboard shows it, to those who may read its history (T354, the version view); and when a proposal shows it, to those who may open the proposal (the review view).
        - From T408's review: at first, `?for=` trusted the named dashboard's body. So anyone with a workspace could put another folder's image id on their own dashboard and read it through that. The save check closes that.
      - `GET /api/introspection/sources` listed every data source Cube has, and `…/:source/{schemas,tables,columns,scaffold}` read any source's catalog with the service credential, for any signed-in user.
        - Now a user browses only a data source they may see (AC-263): Cube's name for it is its connection's (`connectionNameOf`). Cube's own `default` is the root's.
        - A name that is neither is a Super-Admin's alone, since what it reads isn't known here (T408's review: it first fell back to the root's, open to every writer).
        - Any other source is refused before Cube is asked.
      - `POST /api/jobs/queries/find` returned anyone's query records by request id. It now returns the user's own, and a Super-Admin everyone's, as their Jobs lists them (R42.6).
    - **From T408's review, the matrix asks more.**
      - Import and import review are asked with a real file for every target, and so is a file whose dashboard names another folder's image.
      - Build states are asked with every place's token.
      - Schedules are asked both ways (`?seen=1` shows a rollup's name to whoever may see its folder, R42.7, which the matrix now says).
      - The review count must equal what "To review" lists.
      - `default`, a source wechart doesn't know, a kept version's image, a proposal's image and a workspace data source are planted too.
      - No mark is found inside another's: rollups' and tokens' marks end in a letter of their own.
      - Not planted: workspace model files, which workspaces don't hold yet (T347).
    - **Kept as it is, and said.**
      - `GET /api/charts/:id/dashboards` answers `[]` for a chart the user may not open. That is what it answers for no chart, so nothing is told.
      - History is a writer's and a Super-Admin's (T354).
      - A cancel (`DELETE /api/running-query/:id`) always answers 204 (AC-011). The matrix shows Cube is asked it as the user, never as wechart.

## P2.17 The integration plan, wechart's side, slice by slice (added 2026-09-26)

These tasks carry out wechart's column of the plan's slices (`docs/inputs/2026-09-26-integration-plan.md`, "Slices"). Each depends on the xcube routes its slice brings, which the Cube side builds and the user brings over. Routes the plan's contract lacks are proposed on the plan doc's contract section first: the JWKS push, and the build-event record.

The IDs T424, T434 and T439 are unused; no task carries them.

Most tests here run against a **stub xcube** (`packages/api/src/xcube/fake.ts`), a server that records every call and answers as the contract says. Each slice's end-to-end test runs against compose's Cube once it runs xcube's slice.

Slice 7 is optional in the plan and has no criterion, so it has no task. It would use Cube's own answers in place of the rules wechart re-implements. *(2026-09-28, R39: deferred past phase 2, with aliasing a file-set model's JavaScript, Jinja and Python cubes on a changed target; `docs/phase-2/backlog.md` §7.)* The plan's runbook (slice 8) has no criterion either; either can be proposed as a spec change when the user wants it.

### Slice 2: foundation

- [x] T418 [P] (AC-319) Keep publish drafts in the metadata database, so any API replica answers Cube's read-back
  - Why: the drafts `Map` in `model/publish.ts` breaks with two replicas: Cube's read-back can land on the other one (research `cube/ha-topology.md`, table row 1). This is interim until ~~slice 3~~ slice 2's cut-over removes the read-back (T431; `[R29]`).
  - Files: a migration `…_publish-drafts.cjs`, `packages/api/src/db/schema.ts`, `packages/api/src/model/drafts.ts` (the store), `packages/api/src/model/publish.ts`, `packages/api/src/server.ts` and `packages/api/src/main.ts` (wiring), `packages/api/src/model/publish-drafts.test.ts`
  - Failing test: `publish-drafts.test.ts`: with two API instances on one database, a publish started through one has its draft read by Cube's callback through the other. No draft is held in a process's memory (AC-319).
  - Depends on: none
  - **Done 2026-09-26.**
    - **The store.** Drafts are in a `publish_drafts` table: a text id, the files as jsonb, a read flag and a timestamp. The id is text because it arrives in a URL, and a malformed one is a draft that isn't there. `main.ts` wires the database store; `buildServer` keeps an in-memory one for tests without a database.
    - **The test failed first on the behaviour.** With the store wired but publishing still on its own map, it gave 502: the other replica didn't have the draft. It then passed.
      - Cube's read-back through the other replica answers 200, the publish lands, and that draft's row is gone.
      - A Cube that answers without reading the draft is still refused with 502, and leaves no row.
      - A malformed or missing draft id is a 404.
    - **Runs.** The publishing specs passed in Chrome against compose's Cube: `publish-model`, `generate-cubes`, `data-source` and `save-to-folder`.
    - **The cold review (PASS)** led to:
      - the not-read case against the database store;
      - asserting the read-back's status in the test, rather than inside the fake Cube, where a failure was swallowed;
      - checking this draft's own row rather than the whole table, which outlives a run;
      - the malformed-id case.
    - **Left as is:**
      - a process that dies mid-publish leaves its draft row behind, unread, until slice 3 removes drafts (T431);
      - the chart's `replicas: 1` comment in `api.yaml` names the draft map, and T423 rewrites it.
    - AC-319 stays open (T421–T423, T444).

  - **Done 2026-09-26, against the stub.**
    - **Where xcube is configured**, a publish is checked by one `PUT …/snapshot?dryRun=true` per 1,000 probes in place of the draft Cube read back. Its order is the draft path's:
      1. the model compiles;
      2. no rollup names a member the model lacks (AC-189);
      3. every refresh-key cron is one Cube runs;
      4. every cube with rollups plans (AC-235).

      Only then is it written, sent (T419), and the metadata cache cleared. Without xcube the draft path is unchanged, so both suites run as before until T447.
    - **What is refused and what fails:**
      - A model that doesn't compile is refused (422), each error on its file, line and column. An error xcube places on no file is placed by `placeOf`, and with no errors at all Cube's own text is parsed as before.
      - A file xcube won't take is refused on that file.
      - A probe's 400 refuses the publish, naming the rollup, its file and Cube's reason, whether or not the change touched it (R29: every break refuses).
      - Any other probe answer, a probe with no answer, or xcube unreachable publishes nothing and says so (502).
    - **What the tests show.** `check.test.ts` (11), through the publish route against the stub:
      - the one call, its files, context and probes, with no `compare`;
      - each kind of refusal above, with its message;
      - the order (an unknown member is named before its probe's 500);
      - that nothing reaches the store, `afterPublish` or the draft store for a refused publish.
    - **The cold review (FAIL)** led to:
      - An unknown member's 500 was answered 502 before AC-189's check; the checks now run in the draft path's order.
      - A probe missing from xcube's answer passed; it now publishes nothing.
      - Columns were dropped; they are kept.
      - Failures to reach xcube weren't logged; they are.
      - The probes had no cap; they go in batches of 1,000, xcube's limit.
      - A refused file was placed on every changed file; it is placed on the one xcube names.
      - The tests that were missing were added.
    - **Left:** AC-136 and AC-235 stay as they are until T447 runs this against xcube itself. The Jinja-tagged file in the refused-file test becomes T446's case, since T446 sends no such file.

  - *As built (2026-09-30, from the paused stash "T437 wip", on a branch of its own beside the main session):*
    - **Signing** (`cube/signing.ts`): every query token is RS256 under the API's signing key, its `kid` the key's RFC 7638 thumbprint, security on or off. A token carries `role: user`, `aud: xcube`, `iss: wechart`, `iat`, `exp` (an hour at most), `groups`, `wechartModel` and `wechartRevision`, and nothing else. Until the key set is pushed the client signs HS256 as before, but the start pushes it before the API listens.
    - **The groups** (`cube/named-groups.ts`, `CubeClient.as(user, named)`): with sign-in on, a user's token carries only their groups that some access policy in the model names (`group`/`groups`, not `*`) or that a folder's allowed set holds. That is every group granted on a folder, and the Super-Admin group. The folders' groups are read for each token, as access checks read them. The model's policy groups are read again when the recorded revision moves, or after a minute. A preview carries exactly its chosen groups (AC-166); the configured context with sign-in off is untrimmed.
    - **The key push** (`xcube/keys.ts`): the public half only, through `PUT …/keys` with the service credential, at the version one above what xcube holds (`GET …/keys`), so replicas with one set push it at one version. **No wechart table:** the stash's `xcube_key_sets` migration is dropped, since xcube holds the version, and a migration here would clash in order with the main session's on the shared test databases (a small decision, reported).
      - At start, nothing is sent when xcube holds every key of the API's, beside others or not. So an API still configured with one key, restarted while others rotate, leaves their next key in place (the review's finding).
      - A rotation (`WECHART_SIGNING_NEXT_KEY`) pushes the current and next keys, signs with the next once that push is answered, and after an hour and a minute pushes exactly the next.
      - A concurrent push's `409 stale_keys` or `conflict` is accepted when the held set holds the API's keys; otherwise the start stops. It is never retried with the old set.
    - **Settings:** `WECHART_SIGNING_KEY` (or `_FILE`) is required with `WECHART_XCUBE_MODEL`. It must not be the service key, which xcube refuses to take pushed. The development key is `infra/xcube/dev-signing-key.pem`. The chart generates a 4096-bit key once into the Secret (`signing-key.pem`, `genPrivateKey "rsa"`) and gives it to the API alone. Compose runs no API, so `docker-compose.yml` needs no key: xcube learns it from the push.

- [x] T464 (AC-201, AC-013) Keep a tile's title whole, moving its badges to the foot whenever the head can't hold both
  - Files: `packages/web/src/tiles/badgePlace.ts`, `packages/web/src/tiles/Tile.tsx` (+ tests), `e2e/tile-head.spec.ts`
  - *As built:*
    - **The cause.** Flex shrinking shares a loss between everything that can shrink. So whenever the freshness badge shrank, the title lost a fraction of a pixel too: it needed 73.64 px and was drawn at 73.31 px, so its ellipsis showed ("Custome…"). `roomIn`'s 0.5 px slack then read the −0.33 px as fitting, and the badge kept the head.
    - **The fix, in `shell/styles.ts`:** while a badge shares the head, the title doesn't shrink (`flex-shrink: 0`). The badge alone gives way. Once even its least width doesn't fit, `roomIn` goes below 0 and the badges move.
    - **Review fix:** in `badgePlace.ts` and `tiles/ChartTile.tsx`, badges in the foot come back once the head has room for what the foot holds now (`badgesNeeded`: the freshness badge at its least width). Before, they waited for room for all that left with them, so an "Updating…" or a marking that had gone kept the rest in the foot.
    - **The e2e** also checks that a badge in the head fits and a badge in the foot had no room.
    - **Fonts:** there is no `@font-face`, so no font loads late. The test measures after `document.fonts.ready`.
    - **Side effect:** `editor-preview.spec.ts` "a tile resized in this session…" passes again, because that tile's badge now stays in its head. The preview's chart has no foot, so a tile whose badges are in its foot would still preview 26 px taller.
    - **Found failing at HEAD, not T464's:** `markings.spec.ts` "Invert marking and Mark all…" (3 of 6 alone).
  - Failing test: `tile-head.spec.ts`:

Also refused whole: an empty file, one that doesn't say it is a wechart export, one with no list of items, and a newer export version.
    - **Parts (state K):** every item is checked before any is taken, and each refusal names the part and why, as the design words it:
      - a kind other than dashboard, chart, model or data source;
      - a chart type, or a tile's intended chart type, not in `render-spec.ts`;
      - a driver or sign-in method this wechart lacks;
      - a chart this wechart can't read, upgraded first where it is older;
      - a data source holding any of its driver's secrets, a setting its driver has no field for, or a name a data source can't take;
      - a model path xcube wouldn't take;
      - not exactly one dashboard, an own chart of a dashboard the file doesn't hold, a second chart of an id, a second data source of a name, a second model of a path.

    - **Small decisions, overturnable:**
      - A newer export *version* is refused whole. It marks a format change, which design 13's "no version gate" (between wechart releases) doesn't reach.

Every surface here follows design 14 (R48), drawn before the UI tasks start. The API halves of T517–T521 depend on nothing else.

*Design 14 approved 2026-09-30 (R49), with its proposals P1 (a folder row's second line shows its description, AC-369) and P2 (the kind in the address, AC-370). Its questions were answered:*

- [x] T542 (AC-281, AC-323) Rebind a workspace item's stored names to the workspace's own cube in its previews *(added 2026-10-01, `[R53]`: "Rebind in the workspace")*
  - Files: `packages/api/src/xcube/overlays.ts` and the query route's workspace branch in `server.ts` (`POST …/resolve` with `overlay`), `e2e/security/workspace-overlay.spec.ts`
  - Failing test: a tile saved against a path's `orders`, then a workspace cube `orders` made to land elsewhere: the tile's preview answers from the workspace's cube; landed, it binds where it lands (AC-281).

  - *As built (2026-10-01):*
    - **Rebinding** (`packages/api/src/access/rebind.ts`):
      - In the previews of a workspace item, and of a proposal, each name the query holds is resolved again by its short name against the overlay's own cubes and views. The overlay is the one the scope already ensured.
      - Where the overlay holds one of that short name, wherever it places it, that one is asked; otherwise the stored name is kept.
      - This is xcube's overlay-first rule (research `xcube-slice-5.md`, "POST …/resolve with overlay"), applied to the overlay's content as pushed. **Small decision, overturnable:** no `resolve` round trip. The overlay holds one item of a short name, so the content answers it exactly.

      - Cube's answer is put back under the names the item asked: each row, the annotation, the echoed `query` and `pivotQuery`, and each of `results`. So tiles read it as they always did.
        - This works member by member. A query naming a member both ways (a chart drawn before the workspace's cube, given a member after) asks it once, and is answered under both names.
        - A time dimension's grain keys (`….ordered_at.month`) follow their member.
      - `/api/load`, `/api/sql` and `/api/acceleration` rebind before the scope check, which checks the names actually asked. The acceleration panel's member that stops a rollup comes back under the stored name. Its rollup ids, and Cube's errors, name the workspace's cube.
      - A shared item opened by itself is queried as it was, since its scope has no overlay. A shared library chart shown on a workspace dashboard is rebound with the dashboard's previews, which is AC-281's "the workspace's own cube of that name answers there too".
    - **AC-285 is unchanged** (T542's review): a model goes with a proposed item only where the item names the full name the model makes. An approval binds the item where it lands (T502), so a model placed off the name's folder is never what the landed item uses, and bundling it would only hold the proposal at T451's 503 and freeze the model. The proposal's review shows what would land. A tile drawn once the workspace's cube was made names that cube, so its model goes, and the proposal's previews rebind through it.
    - **Landed, it binds where it lands** (the failing test's last clause): an approval binds a chart's names by short name, nearest first from the folder it lands in (T502, `proposal-bind.test.ts`). For an item rebound in the workspace, that is shown once T451 lands proposals holding models.

## P2.21 The SQL runner (F40, added 2026-10-01, `[R50]`)

Read-only SQL on a data source's own connection, or on Cube Store, through xcube, which alone opens the credential. Asked of xcube in `~/Work/xcube-exchange/to-xcube/2026-10-01-0057-sql-runner.md`.

*xcube answered with `ghcr.io/senthilkrajagopal/xcube:v1.7.45-89628a0e88@sha256:155d204c…7a4d17` (`to-wechart/2026-10-01-1200-sql-runner-built.md`). It provides:*
- *`POST …/connections/{name}/sql`, with `?overlay=<id>` for a workspace's own data source, named `<folderId>__<name>`;*
- *`POST …/cubestore/sql`, SELECT and EXPLAIN only;*
- *`POST …/sql/cancel`, which reaches the instance running the run.*

*Things to know: many drivers return numbers as strings, every SQL Server number among them; column types are the database's own names, and null on Cube Store; a database's error can quote the SQL's values.*

*Design 15 was approved 2026-10-01 with P1–P5 and its answers (R51). AC-373, AC-374, AC-378 … AC-381, AC-383 … AC-385 were amended, and AC-386 and AC-387 added.*

      - when the data source is deleted, its switch goes too.

    - **The route.** `POST /api/data-sources/:id/sql` `{ sql }` (`routes/sql-runner.ts`, registered with the data sources' routes):
      - **Who:** one rule, `mayRunSql`, for the run and the tab (T535):
        - a shared folder's data source: write access to its folder (a Super-Admin, or its own folder's read-write members; one who sees it from a folder below has none), and its switch on;
        - one in My workspace: its owner, the only one who sees it, with no switch, unless it is a copy pointed elsewhere (below).
      - **Refusals:** `403` with why: the runner is off, or not theirs; `404` for one they can't see. Each is decided before anything reaches xcube.
      - **The run:** a fresh run id, the SQL (1–100,000 characters) and R50's caps (10,000 rows, 30,000 ms, 10 MB).
        - A shared one runs on its connection, `<xcube folder id>__<name>`.
        - A workspace's runs on its workspace's overlay (`?overlay=`), made sure of first (T347), under its original's folder or its target's.
      - **Answers:** `{ outcome: 'finished', columns, rows, rowCount, truncated, durationMs, statement }`, or, with its status:
        - `refused` (400): "Only SELECT and EXPLAIN run here, one statement at a time.", with xcube's reason and the kind found;
        - `timeout` or `cancelled` (422);
        - `failed`: the database's message (422), or "Couldn't connect…" (502);
        - `busy` (503, `Retry-After: 5`);
        - `unavailable` (409, or 503 with xcube away).
        - xcube's `redactedSql` isn't sent to the browser; T534 keeps it.

      - Such a copy needs the switch, and `PUT …/sql-runner` now takes one for it.
      - **In effect it can't run until landed:** no Super-Admin sees another user's workspace, so only a Super-Admin's own copy can be switched on. The refusal says so: "…No Super-Admin can see your workspace, so propose it: once it's approved and landed, a Super-Admin can turn it on there."
    - **Small decisions, overturnable:**
      - a copy whose original is gone needs the switch, since it can't be compared;
      - with sign-in off, a workspace's data source has no preview (no overlays), so a run on it says so (`409`);
      - a change of the way of signing in counts as repointed.
